text: The Store Ops page is done. Now it's time to build the second page in this same Power BI model -- for the Regional Manager, on gold.category_breakdown, the Gold table built back in Lesson 7 specifically because the existing table couldn't answer this question.

Go back to Lesson 1. The Regional Manager's actual ask was: I want to see which categories are driving that number, and whether that's different store to store. That's not a time question the way Store Ops' question is -- it's a composition question. Of the sales a store generated, how much came from which category. gold.daily_sales_summary was never built to answer this, because it has no category dimension at all.

This page needs three things. A bar chart of total_sales by category -- bars, not a line, because the question isn't about a trend over time, it's about comparing a handful of discrete categories against each other at a glance. A store_id slicer, since the question explicitly asks whether the mix differs store to store. And a sale_date slicer, letting the Regional Manager filter to this quarter or compare against last quarter without turning the bar chart into a trend chart it was never meant to be.

Notice what's different from the Store Ops page, on purpose. There, sale_date was the chart's main axis, because that question was about watching a number move over time. Here, category is the main axis, because this question is about composition -- how sales break down -- not about a number changing over time. Date moves from being the subject of the chart to just a filter on it.

That's the same design instinct both pages follow. Whatever dimension a question is actually about becomes the chart's main axis. Whatever dimension is just there to focus the view -- pick one store, pick one quarter -- becomes a slicer. Same model, same underlying pipeline, two genuinely different pages because two genuinely different questions were asked.

Both stakeholders now have a real report page, built on validated Gold data. But validation isn't a one-time event -- it's lesson nine's reconciliation query, waiting to be run again. Next lesson, the numbers stop matching, and you'll find out why.
